# git-idm

git-idm sets the git author, the SSH key, the signing key and the GitHub (gh) login from the folder of the repo. git and gh follow the folder in every shell, your shells too. You do not switch identities.

## Before you commit or push

Run `git-idm` in the repo. It shows the identity of this folder.

- "no identity here": stop. Tell the user. Do not bind the folder yourself.
- "override": a `git-idm use` from the shell that started you is active. Tell the user before you commit or push.
- Any other identity: continue.

## When git-idm stops a command

A stop message starts with "git-idm blocked:" or "git-idm:" and has a "fix:" line.

1. Stop. Do not try to go around the check.
2. Show the message and the fix line to the user.
3. Run a fix only when the user tells you to.

## Never do these

- `git commit --no-verify` or `git push --no-verify`.
- `GIT_IDM_GH_CHECK=0 gh ...`.
- Set `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` or `GIT_SSH`.
- `git -c credential.helper=...` or `git -c core.sshCommand=...`.
- Put a token or a user name in a remote URL.
- Change the author: `git config user.name` or `user.email`, `--author`, `GIT_AUTHOR_*` or `GIT_COMMITTER_*`. Do this only when the user tells you to.
- Run `git-idm bind`, `unbind`, `use`, `allow`, `guard`, `edit`, `rm`, `migrate` or `login`. Do this only when the user tells you to.

## Commands only the user can run

- `git-idm accept`: approves the commits that a blocked push stopped, when they use another identity on purpose. It asks on the terminal, so you cannot run it. Ask the user to run it, then push again.
- `git-idm login <identity>`: logs gh in again when a token stops working.

## Commands you can run

- `git-idm`: show the identity of this folder.
- `git-idm ls`: list the identities.
- `git-idm doctor`: find problems. It changes nothing.
